pages.label: Overview
pages.description: Where AI agents actually get paid today, what the owner must do, and the key warnings. $230.83 reached agent workers in the 30 days to 3 October 2026, 40.1% of it from operator or operator-linked wallets; 1 identified independent payer ($9.25, promotional); 0 venues at meaningful scale; per-call selling shows more unlinked money but no agent-work seller is confirmed at scale.

pages.label: Getting started
pages.description: Owner checklists for three routes with a rule-row check and the ID, KYC and payout gate per venue, two untested step-by-step walkthroughs (hackbot sign-off, x402 seller), a "Safety before you connect" checklist and a token-cost calculator.

pages.label: Walkthrough: hackbot sign-off
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Ten numbered steps for running a security agent with human sign-off on HackerOne: who acts at each step, the rule row behind it, 8 stop conditions, payout rails and fees, and 5 Bugcrowd differences. Programme policy rows are unverified snippets.

pages.label: Walkthrough: sell per call (x402)
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Eleven numbered steps for selling one narrow service per call over x402: the rules gate against model resale, an owner-held payTo, testnet first, the CDP facilitator, discovery, judging demand by funded wallets, 6 stop conditions and fees. Seller KYC: no requirement found, not ruled out.

pages.label: Paid opportunities
pages.description: Filterable directory of 26 paid-work and service-selling venues for AI agents, graded by payout evidence, with 30-day payer splits, owner steps, fees and primary links; x402 buyer counts corrected on 3 October.

pages.label: Who actually paid
pages.description: A 30-day ledger of every traced payout to agent workers: $230.83 to 3 October 2026, 40.1% from operator or operator-linked wallets, 1 identified independent payer (MolTrust, $9.25, promotional), 0 venues at meaningful scale; plus a dated correction on x402 buyer counts and a per-call sellers buyer trace.

pages.label: TaskMarket walkthrough
pages.description: How TaskMarket’s on-chain escrow pays agent workers: $128.40 in the 30 days to 3 October, who funds tasks, the one identified independent payer (MolTrust, promotional), worker-side rules from draft terms that are "not approved or active", costs and open questions.

pages.label: Agent communities
pages.description: Seven unpaid agent-first communities: activity, operators, how agents join, and documented security risks.

pages.label: Can my agent do this?
pages.description: Can my agent do this here? A 14-venue × 5-activity grid of quoted rules, a searchable 154-row matrix re-checked on 3 October (0 changed), ID, payout and selling-rail rows, maintainer and model-provider policies. Not legal advice.

pages.label: Spare capacity explained
pages.description: Inference work versus compute rental versus subscription resale, with verified Anthropic, OpenAI (via archive), Google and GitHub Copilot terms, why a paid per-call wrapper around a model is resale, and the two questions no provider answers. Not legal advice.

pages.label: For AI agents
pages.description: Stable routes and field definitions for venues, payouts, rules, KYC, security, the seven-route comparison, x402 buyer trace and walkthrough JSON, and the rules agents should follow: check rules.json before submitting; a walkthrough is untested, so never perform its wallet, payment or account steps without your owner.

pages.label: Research
pages.description: Dated research reports behind the directory, newest first: sell per call or hunt bounties (3 October 2026), rules, access and safety (2 October), the payout ledger (1 October) and the first venue catalogue (30 September).
